excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
<@785811170387951616> , this is the config for Prysm only testing with the Prysm image doing subnet sampling only.
(I tested if for ~10 hours in a raw without issue.)

```yaml
participants:
  # Super nodes
  - cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:peerDAS-4a731d8
    vc_image: gcr.io/prysmaticlabs/prysm/validator:stable
    count: 2
    cl_max_mem: 4096
    cl_extra_params: 
      - --subscribe-all-subnets
      - --p2p-max-peers=4
      - --minimum-peers-per-subnet=1

  # Full nodes
  - cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:peerDAS-4a731d8
    vc_image: gcr.io/prysmaticlabs/prysm/validator:stable
    count: 3
    cl_max_mem: 4096
    cl_extra_params: 
      - --p2p-max-peers=4
      - --minimum-peers-per-subnet=1

network_params:
  eip7594_fork_epoch: 0
  eip7594_fork_version: "0x50000038"

snooper_enabled: true
global_log_level: debug

additional_services:
  - dora
  - prometheus_grafana
  - goomy_blob

dora_params:
  image: ethpandaops/dora:peerdas-as-deneb

ethereum_metrics_exporter_enabled: true
```

Not really sure to understand the question, but a Prysm full node is subscribed to `get_custody_columns(node_id, subnet_sampling_size) = 8` subnets. When looking for peers, the node will try to find peers subscribed (among other) to these 8 subnets.

> it means 52, 54,55 were missed
Got it thanks. So if I understand well:
-  1 `[empty]` on column `51` means column `52` is missed
- 2 `[empty]`s on column `53` means columns `54` and `55` are missed.

> I have a feeling that it could be due to lack of resources on one of the sides
My intuition is our gossipsub library is silently stopping sending columns to teku because, for some reason, the gossip score of the teku peer is too low.
 (I have to confirm by activating the trace logs of the gossipsub library that floods 1 million messages/sec...)

Also, to add more context, for this precise block:
- A prysm full node published the block, but withheld on purpose columns 0 to 63
- A prysm super node then reconstructed (at 3 seconds into the slot) all the missing 0 to 63 columns and reseeded them to the network. The majority of them was received by the teku node, but some... not.
